title: Replace a bicycle brake pad
learner_outcome: Replace one rim-brake pad on a bicycle, then verify the brake by hand before riding. The brake model is not identified in this course, so the learner fetches the manufacturer's manual for their own brake and takes the pad model, fastener and torque values from it.
through_line: One brake pad, one fastener at a time: read the manual, loosen only the named fastener, seat the new pad, then prove the brake works by hand before the wheel turns.
prerequisite_assumptions: The learner has the bicycle and its manufacturer's manual in front of them.
The learner can identify a rim brake and the pad that presses on the rim.

time_estimate.rationale: One 45-minute session covers the four steps of this single procedure: identify the pad, remove the worn pad, seat and tighten the new pad, verify the brake by hand. The four sections are steps inside that one session, not four separate sessions. No attainment figure is claimed because completion is verified, not learned.

objectives.title: Identify the correct replacement pad for the brake model
evidence_criteria: The pad model printed in the manual for this brake is written down

objectives.title: Remove the worn pad without damaging the caliper
evidence_criteria: The worn pad is removed with the fastener the manual names
A photo of the worn pad beside the loosened fastener is taken for the learner's own record

objectives.title: Seat and tighten the new pad to the manual's specification
evidence_criteria: The new pad is seated square in the caliper
The fastener is tightened to the torque printed in the manual for this brake model

objectives.title: Verify the brake by hand before riding
evidence_criteria: A second person confirms the lever is firm
The wheel spins without rubbing after the new pad is fitted

sections.title: Identify the pad
sections.lesson_intent: Match the pad model and the caliper fastener to the manufacturer's labelled parts diagram before touching the brake.

media_need.construct: The labelled parts diagram: pad model, pad slot and the single caliper mounting fastener

context_needs: the manufacturer's manual for the learner's brake model
the manual's labelled diagram of the caliper

sections.title: Remove the worn pad
sections.lesson_intent: Follow the labelled sequence for releasing the caliper fastener and sliding the worn pad out without damaging the caliper.

media_need.construct: The labelled diagram showing the sequence of steps that release the caliper fastener and free the pad

context_needs: the manufacturer's manual for the learner's brake model
the hex key the manual names for the caliper fastener

sections.title: Seat and tighten
sections.lesson_intent: Seat the new pad square in the caliper and tighten the fastener to the torque the manual prints for this brake model.

media_need.construct: The labelled parts diagram showing pad orientation and seating before the fastener is tightened

context_needs: the manufacturer's manual for the learner's brake model
the torque value the manual prints for the caliper fastener

sections.title: Verify by hand
sections.lesson_intent: Run the manual's hand-verification steps and have a second person confirm the lever and the free wheel before any ride.

media_need.construct: The labelled diagram of the parts that move when the brake lever is squeezed

context_needs: the manufacturer's manual for the learner's brake model
a second person to confirm the hand check

check_plan.notes: The learner writes down the pad model read from their own manual; the photo the learner takes for objective 2 shows the same pad.

The checklist asks the learner to confirm the named fastener and the photo of the worn pad beside it. The attempt records that confirmation as self-reported; the photo stays the learner's own record, and no upload lane exists in this build.
The torque value is read from the learner's manual; the course states none, and the checklist asks the learner to confirm the fastener was tightened to that printed value.
The checklist asks the learner to confirm a second person checked the lever and the free wheel. That confirmation is recorded as the learner's self-report, never as independent evidence.

context_needs: the manufacturer's manual for the learner's brake model
the hex key the manual names for the caliper fastener
a work stand or a way to hold the bicycle steady
a camera to photograph the removed pad
a second person for the hand verification
exclusions: Does not cite or supply a manufacturer manual; the learner must fetch the manual for their own brake model.
Does not state a pad model, fastener size or torque value as fact; the example's model and key are stand-ins for what the learner's manual prints.
Does not certify the procedure; the manufacturer's documentation and an expert check remain the authority.
No live-road test is part of this brief.
Not for hydraulic, disc or e-bike brake systems.
evidence_note: No manufacturer manual was fetched for this course. The brake model is unknown here, all four objectives are marked unverified, and no pad model, fastener size or torque value is stated as fact. The example's pad model and key are stand-ins for the values printed in the learner's own manual.
